fit: standardized saffron extract and DASS depression outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The adjusted between-arm improvement was 2.37 points (95% CI 0.23 to 4.51). Standardized extract, selected non-Parkinson population and sponsor involvement limit transfer.

fit: rosemary extract shared by two fish oil and comparator capsule arms
assessment: PHQ-8 change was inconclusive between arms. Both groups took rosemary extract, leaving its contribution unidentified.

fit: rosemary essential oil among 15 odors in a dementia pilot
assessment: All three groups had a median GDS of zero after treatment. Posttest group comparison was inconclusive. No assigned rosemary-only or culinary exposure.

fit: mixed essential-oil massage containing rosemary and HADS depression
assessment: Results report a favorable blend-plus-massage depression contrast. Baseline group imbalance and inconsistent baseline statistics limit interpretation. Neither rosemary nor ingestion was isolated.

fit: inhaled distilled rosemary oil and Zung depression scores
assessment: Posttest group comparison favored oil over waiting list. Pre-existing class allocation, route and absence of Parkinson disease rule out an isolated fresh-leaf ingestion interpretation.

fit: secondary pooled review of oral and inhaled rosemary and depressive symptoms
assessment: The author abstract reports inconclusive pooled depression and high heterogeneity. Oral subgroup anxiety is a different outcome. Depression forest plots and full study table are open.

fit: perimenopausal fatigue after standardized saffron extract
assessment: Preprint reports POMS fatigue changes of minus 7.6 and minus 1.7 points; interaction p=.0003. Different formulation, scale and clinical population limit transfer.

fit: five-odor training including cinnamon and postinfectious olfaction
assessment: Group-by-time TDI comparison favored odor training (p=.018). Multiple combined odors, no oral exposure or Parkinson cohort, and unresolved item-level reporting discrepancy.
